Use counts.tsv. For rows whose samples.csv value_type is 'relative (%)', convert to counts as round(value × n_counted / 100). Compute raw-count Bray–Curtis for all sample pairs and report the mean.

If every core's 63–150 µm fraction was picked, sum each core's two fractions per taxon and compute Shannon (natural log). Otherwise the >63 µm assemblage is not observed for some cores: compute Shannon on the >150 µm fraction alone for every core in both campaigns. Report the mean per campaign.

Rename each counts.tsv column to its taxonomy.csv accepted_name (exact recorded string) and sum columns that share an accepted name. Richness is the number of accepted names with a nonzero total. Mean Bray–Curtis on the merged raw counts over all sample pairs.

Map each lab_number to its core via register.csv and sum the counts of a core's lab numbers. Convert each core to relative abundances and run one-way PERMANOVA (Bray–Curtis) with zone as the factor, cores as units; report pseudo-F, R² and n.

Build the age model from dates.csv rows with status 'accepted' only, interpolating linearly (extrapolating linearly from the nearest two dates beyond the dated range). Keep samples younger than 11,700 cal BP; mean Bray–Curtis on relative abundances over their pairs; report the mean and the count.
